memo.verdict: Neutral on the shares at 17,430p (2026-09-24); bullish on the case below about 16,200p (the eighteen-month bar at the blended 22.8x multiple) and with conviction below about 14,700p (the three-year bar). Progress, not park: no D or F sits on management ('Operator quality' A), business quality ('Business' A), predictability ('No fundamental shocks' C with the outcome skew at B) or trackability ('Leading indicators' B), so the park rule does not apply; the technical gate (D) says the price is not yet ours to buy and the two entry levels say where it becomes so. Conviction medium, a working hypothesis on the volume condition until the H1 FY2027 results and first FY2027 floor on 12 January 2027; high on the foundations. The record's one-line bet: a company that absorbed £12 million of tariffs while expanding its gross margin in a fallow year will grow core revenue 9 percent and hold a 39 percent core operating margin in its edition year with new capacity, and a three-broker consensus modelling two flat years is corrected by the January 2027 floor; the record is not betting on the multiple, which is why it does not buy at 17,430p.
case: - Games Workshop is a compounder case at the wrong price. The business is an extreme positive outlier and the edition year, new capacity and a dense licensing pipeline should lift EPS about 10 percent a year against a consensus that models two flat years; at 17,430p the shares already pay 26.5 times consensus earnings for that, so the modal return is 13 to 14 percent a year against the 20 percent bar, and the case clears the bar only below about 16,200p.

- The change is real, specific, dated and modest: the edition-year re-acceleration of a business that grew core revenue 10.9 percent in a fallow year while paying £12 million of new tariffs. The 11th Edition has been in the market since June 2026; Factory 4 doubles the capacity that rationed a £405.3 million trade channel; the Chief Operating Officer unifies design and manufacture against the allocation bottleneck; Dawn of War IV and Total War keep licensing growing from £32.9 million. The external forces net to a mild cost headwind, not a demand inflection; tabletop games grow 5.00 percent a year.

- The change has travelled through resources (the Chief Operating Officer, the Group Finance Director, country managers in Shanghai and Seoul), choices (Factory 4, Sawley, the £120 million buffer), actions (the launch, the October 2025 price rise, 30 new stores), the key operating metrics (trade accounts +12 percent; trade revenue +17.2 percent) and the financial statements (core operating profit +15.7 percent; core gross margin +160 basis points; profit before tax £275.7 million against a £265 million floor), and has stopped at the sell-side's estimates: consensus EPS £6.37 for both FY2027 and FY2028 against £6.22, consensus EBIT flat at £281 million against £277 million.
counter_case: - This is a fully valued compounder whose growth is normalising, and the market has begun to say so. FY2026 EPS grew 4.9 percent; the second half's £3.04 was below the prior year's £3.06; second-half core revenue growth was about 5 percent and December 2025 was only slightly ahead; the licensing line has re-based to £32.9 million and the next games run to the licensees' timetables, not the company's; consensus models flat earnings for two years and two of the three visible brokers model FY2027 total revenue growth of 3 to 5 percent.

- Every FY2027 cost line is adverse: tariffs £13 million, plastic £2 million, a stronger pound, 30 store openings, a £28.0 million Sawley lease from FY2026/27, an ERP cut-over in North America in summer 2027; and management itself holds a £120 million buffer against its going-concern stress scenarios.
triggers: - The test of the volume and margin conditions together: the H1 FY2027 results and first FY2027 floor on 12 January 2027. A floor below £290 million of profit before tax changes the record's mind on the upgrade; H1 FY2027 core growth below 5 percent is the alarm on the exit rate; a negative H1 FY2027 core revenue growth print invalidates.

- Core volume: the Jefferies Retail Trends Barometer below zero for two consecutive months (alarm); MyWarhammer actives flat (alarm), down 10 percent with double-digit reported growth (invalidate, the price-not-volume trigger); trade accounts flat (alarm), falling (invalidate); fill rates still below half once Factory 4 is running (invalidate); an annual price rise above 7.50 percent or inventory provisions above 15 percent (alarm).
- The margin: core operating margin below 38 percent for a half (alarm), below 37 percent (invalidate); the same levels serve the tariff and input-cost risk.

- The upgrade: FactSet consensus FY2027 EPS below £6.20 (alarm), below £6.00 (invalidate); the record's modal case is consensus moving toward £6.81 for FY2027 and £7.51 for FY2028 within twelve months.

- The multiple: the case clears the bar below about 16,160p (eighteen months) and 14,660p (three years) at the blend; the uncleared branch (42 percent) is a 19.9x multiple, −25 percent on unchanged earnings.
- The Amazon series: a confirmed production start or a cast or studio exit changes the view either way; it is outside the modal path and the branch odds.
